QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_22

question.text: What is multilateral netting in the context of clearing and settlement?

answer.text: The clearing corporation nets all buy and sell obligations across all counterparties to arrive at a single net obligation per member
Each pair of trading members bilaterally settles their obligations
The clearing corporation nets positions only within the same trading day
Netting is applied only to futures, not options

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 226 of the NISM Series IV workbook, multilateral netting is used to determine net settlement obligations of each clearing member. Page 238 describes settlement after multilateral netting, producing a single net pay-in or pay-out obligation per member. The Trap: Bilateral netting only considers two parties; multilateral netting considers all parties via the clearing corporation. Netting applies across products covered by the CC, not only futures, and is computed across the relevant settlement cycle for open positions. Note: Source-backed function from pages 226 and 238 of Series IV: multilateral netting reduces gross obligations to a single net pay-in or pay-out per clearing member.
